q: 165. An ideal transition curve is
explain: The clothoid spiral is considered the theoretically ideal transition curve because its curvature increases exactly linearly with distance along the curve, matching the actual path of a vehicle turning at constant speed.

q: 166. Shift of a curve, is
explain: The shift of a curve (the perpendicular distance the circular curve is shifted inward to accommodate a transition curve) is given by the formula L^2/24R, where L is the transition curve length and R the radius.

q: 167. In the prismatic compass
options: the magnetic needle moves with the box
the line of sight doesn't move with the box
the magnetic needle and graduated circle do not move with the box
explain: In a prismatic compass, the magnetic needle (with attached graduated ring) stays fixed relative to magnetic north while the box (and line of sight/sighting vane) rotates freely; so the line of sight does not move with the fixed needle assembly.

q: 168. Local attraction in compass surveying may exist due to
options: incorrect leveling of the magnetic needle
loss of magnetism of the needle
friction of the needle at the pivot
presence of magnetic substances near the instrument
explain: Local attraction is caused by external magnetic disturbances - the presence of magnetic substances (iron objects, power lines, etc.) near the compass station - which deflect the needle from true magnetic north.

q: 169. The horizontal angle between true meridian and magnetic meridian at a place is called
explain: This angle, between the true meridian and the magnetic meridian at a place, is by definition the magnetic declination.

q: 170. Determining the difference in elevation between two points on the surface of the earth, is known as
explain: Leveling, in its most general definition, is the branch of surveying concerned with determining the difference in elevation between points on the earth's surface.

q: 171. When the bubble of the level tube of level, remains central
options: axis of the telescope is horizontal
geometrical axis of the telescope is horizontal
explain: When the bubble is centred (in an adjusted level), the axis of the bubble tube is horizontal, which in turn means the line of sight is horizontal.

q: 172. Plotting of inaccessible points on a plane table, is done by
explain: Points that are inaccessible (cannot be reached to measure distance) but are visible from two known plane table stations are plotted using the intersection method.

q: 173. Locating the position of plane table station with reference to three known points, is known as
explain: When the plane table station's position is determined with reference to three known points visible on the ground, this is specifically termed the three-point problem (a case of resection).

q: 174. The 'fix' of a plane table from three known points, is good, if
options: either the right or left station is nearest
explain: As per the book's answer key, the quality of the 'fix' from three-point resection depends on the geometric configuration (strength of fix relative to the great circle), not simply on which station is nearest, so none of these applies directly.

q: 175. A series of closely spaced contour lines represents a
explain: Closely spaced contour lines indicate a rapid change in elevation over a short horizontal distance, representing a steep slope.

q: 176. Direct method of contouring is
explain: The direct method of contouring, where points actually lying on the contour are located and marked in the field, is the most accurate method, though it is slower than indirect methods.

q: 177. The angle of intersection of a counter and a ridge line, is
explain: Contour lines always cross ridge or valley lines at right angles (90 degrees), since ridge/valley lines represent the direction of steepest slope, which is perpendicular to the contour.

q: 178. In case of double line river, contours are
options: stopped at the banks of the river
stopped at the edge of the river
drawn by parabolic curves having their vertex at the centre of the water
explain: For a double line (wide) river, contours are shown stopping at the edge/bank of the river rather than being drawn across the water body.

q: 179. An imaginary line lying throughout on the surface of the earth and preserving a constant inclination to the horizontal, is called
explain: A contour gradient is an imaginary line on the ground surface that maintains a constant inclination (slope) to the horizontal throughout its length.

q: 180. From any point on the surface with a given inclination
options: only one contour gradient is possible
explain: From any given point with a specified inclination, two contour gradients are geometrically possible - one running in each direction around the slope at that constant grade.

q: 181. Location of contour gradient for a highway is best set out from
explain: For highway alignment, the contour gradient is best set out starting from a saddle (low point on a ridge) and working down the hill, providing more efficient routing options.

q: 182. An angle between the inclined line of sight and the horizontal is called
options: direct angle by angles/distances from same station
by angle from one station/distance from other
by distance from two different stations
by angles from two different stations
explain: Note: this question's answer-key entry appears to be a misprint/mismatch with a different question in the book (locating inaccessible objects); the angle between inclined line of sight and horizontal is properly termed the vertical angle. Please verify this entry visually against your copy.

q: 183. In locating the details of inaccessible objects visible at least from transit stations, the method used is
options: by angles and distances from the same station
by angle from one station and distance from the other station
by distances from two different stations
explain: Note: this answer-key entry appears mismatched with the adjacent question in the book. The standard method for locating inaccessible objects visible from two transit stations is by angles from both stations (intersection); please verify this entry visually against your copy.

q: 184. The traversing by the method of deflection angles is chiefly used in
explain: The deflection angle method of traversing is commonly used across all types of linear engineering works - canals, highways, and railways - since it directly gives the angle by which the alignment changes at each station.

q: 185. The difference between the most probable value and its observed value is
explain: The residual error (or residual) is defined as the difference between the most probable value (usually the mean of observations) and any individual observed value.

q: 186. An arbitrary surface with reference to which the elevation of points are measured and compared, is called
explain: A datum surface is any arbitrarily chosen reference surface (such as mean sea level) from which elevations of points are measured and compared.

q: 187. A line normal to the plumb line at all points is known as
explain: A level line is defined as a curved line that is normal (perpendicular) to the direction of the plumb line (gravity) at every point along its length.

q: 188. Substense bar is an instrument used for
options: measurement of horizontal distances in plane areas
measurement of horizontal distances in undulated areas
explain: A subtense bar is used together with a theodolite to measure horizontal distances indirectly, and it is particularly useful in undulating (uneven) terrain where direct chaining is difficult.

q: 189. The number of horizontal cross wires in a stadia diaphragm is
explain: A standard stadia diaphragm typically has one central horizontal cross wire plus two additional stadia hairs; per the book's answer key, one horizontal wire is noted here (referring to the central sighting hair, distinct from the stadia hairs).

q: 190. A contour map of the area is essential before proceeding with the construction of
explain: A detailed contour map is essential before constructing a dam, since it is critical for determining reservoir capacity, submergence area, and the layout of the dam and spillway.

q: 191. Reciprocal leveling eliminates
options: collimation and curvature error fully and refraction error partly
explain: Reciprocal leveling, by averaging observations taken from both ends of a line, eliminates the combined effects of collimation error, earth's curvature, and atmospheric refraction.

q: 192. Contour lines
explain: Contour lines are always continuous closed loops; they never end abruptly but must eventually close somewhere, either within the map area or by returning to the same elevation elsewhere.

q: 193. Contour lines look to cross each other in case of
explain: Only in the special case of an overhanging cliff can contour lines appear to cross each other in plan view, since one part of the ground overhangs another at a different elevation but same horizontal projection.

q: 194. In a theodolite the line of collimation is
options: parallel to axis of plate levels
explain: For correct theodolite operation, the line of collimation must be perpendicular to the trunnion (horizontal) axis, so that it sweeps out a true vertical plane when the telescope is plunged.

q: 195. In a transit theodolite error due to eccentricity of verniers is counteracted by
options: reading different parts of main scale
taking both right swing and left swing reading
explain: The error due to eccentricity of verniers (misalignment of the vernier scale centre with the instrument's rotation axis) is counteracted by reading both verniers (typically 180 degrees apart) and averaging the results.

q: 196. Right face and left reading are taken to
options: eliminate error of trunnion axis not exactly horizontal
eliminate error in the line of collimation
explain: Taking readings on both faces (face left and face right) of the theodolite and averaging eliminates multiple instrumental errors together - collimation error, trunnion axis error, and other index errors - so all of the above apply.

q: 197. Axis of altitude level is
options: parallel to the line of collimation
explain: The axis of the altitude (vertical circle) level is set parallel to the line of collimation, so that when the bubble is centred, the line of sight reads a true zero (horizontal) on the vertical circle.

q: 198. A 15 cm theodolite means
options: length of the telescope is 15 cm
diameter of lower plate is 15 cm
radius of upper plate is 15 cm
explain: A theodolite is designated by the diameter of its lower (graduated horizontal) plate; a '15 cm theodolite' has a lower plate diameter of 15 cm.

q: 199. A simple circular curve is designated by
options: angle subtended at the centre by a chord of any length
angle subtended at the centre by a chord of particular length
explain: A simple circular curve is designated by its degree of curve, which is the angle subtended at the centre by a chord of a specified (particular) standard length.

q: 200. A fixed point of reference of known elevation is called
explain: A bench mark (BM) is a fixed, stable point of known and recorded elevation used as a reference in leveling operations.

q: 201. An imaginary line tangent to the longitudinal curve of the bubble tube at its middle points is called
explain: This is the definition of the axis of the level tube - the imaginary line tangent to the bubble tube's curved surface at its centre point.

q: 202. The distances AC and BC are measured from two fixed points A and B whose distance AB is known. The point C is plotted by intersection. This method is generally adopted in
explain: Locating an unknown point C by measuring/computing angles or distances from two known points A and B on a fixed baseline, and plotting by intersection, is the basic principle of triangulation.

q: 203. Mistakes which may produce a very serious effect upon the final results arise due to
explain: Serious mistakes in survey work generally result from a combination of human factors - inattention, inexperience, and carelessness - so all of these are valid causes.

q: 204. The systematic errors which persist and have regular effects in the performance of a survey operations, are due to
explain: Systematic errors, which follow a definite mathematical/physical law and persist consistently, typically arise from a faulty (mis-calibrated or maladjusted) instrument.

q: 205. The method of reversal
options: is usually directed to examine whether a certain part is truly parallel or perpendicular to another
makes the erroneous relationship between parts evident
explain: The method of reversal serves both purposes - it examines whether parts of an instrument are truly parallel/perpendicular to each other, and in doing so makes any erroneous relationship between them evident.

q: 206. The apparent error on reversal is
explain: When an instrumental error is examined by the method of reversal, the apparent (observed) error is exactly twice the actual error present in the instrument's adjustment.

q: 207. The sensitivity of bubble tube can be increased by
options: decreasing the radius of curvature of tube
explain: Note: increasing the radius of curvature of the bubble tube generally increases sensitivity in standard theory; however, per the book's printed answer key, decreasing the radius of curvature is given as the answer here - please verify against your copy.

q: 208. With the rise of temperature, the sensitivity of bubble tube
explain: As temperature rises, the liquid inside the bubble tube becomes less viscous and the bubble itself expands, generally reducing the precision/sensitivity of readings, so sensitivity decreases.

q: 209. Refraction correction
options: has no effect on the curvature correction
explain: Atmospheric refraction bends the line of sight in the opposite sense to the effect of earth's curvature, so the refraction correction partially offsets (partially eliminates) the curvature correction, rather than fully cancelling it.

q: 210. While doing leveling in undulating terrain, it is preferable to set level on
explain: In undulating terrain, setting the level instrument on one side of the slope (rather than at the very top or bottom) often provides better command over multiple staff points with fewer instrument setups.

q: 211. A leveling station is a place where
options: both B.S. and F.S. are taken
explain: A leveling station (or instrument station) refers to the point where the leveling instrument itself is physically set up for taking observations.

q: 212. The telescope of a dumpy level
options: is rigidly fixed to the leveling head
can be tilted in a vertical plane
can be taken out of its supports and reversed
permits interchange of eye piece and object glass
explain: In a dumpy level, the telescope is rigidly and permanently fixed to the vertical spindle/leveling head, distinguishing it from tilting or reversible levels.

q: 213. A traverse deflection angle is
options: the difference between the included angle and 180
the difference between 360 and the included angle
explain: A deflection angle is defined as the angle by which a survey line deviates from the prolongation of the preceding line, calculated as the difference between the included angle and 180 degrees.

q: 214. The size of plane table is
explain: A standard plane table board used in surveying is typically 750 mm x 900 mm in size.

q: 215. The vertical distance between any two consecutive contours is called
explain: The constant vertical distance between any two consecutive contour lines on a map is, by definition, the contour interval.

q: 216. The horizontal distance between any two consecutive contours is called
explain: The horizontal distance between two consecutive contours (which varies with the slope) is called the horizontal equivalent.

q: 217. When several contours coincide, it indicates
explain: When multiple contour lines of different elevations coincide (appear as a single line) on a map, it indicates a vertical cliff, where elevation changes without any horizontal distance.

q: 218. A branch of surveying in which the horizontal and vertical distances of points are obtained by instrumental observations, is known as
explain: Tacheometric surveying is defined as the branch in which both horizontal and vertical distances are obtained rapidly through instrumental (stadia) observations, without chaining.

q: 219. The principle of tacheometry is used
options: for filling in detail in topographic surveys
explain: Tacheometry's principle of rapid indirect distance/elevation measurement is widely applied for locating contours, hydrographic surveys, and filling in topographic detail - so all of these apply.

q: 220. The multiplying constant for the tacheometer is
explain: The multiplying constant of a tacheometer is given by f/i, where f is the focal length of the objective and i is the interval between the stadia hairs.

q: 221. The additive constant for the tacheometer is
explain: The additive constant of a tacheometer equals f+d, where f is the focal length of the objective and d is the distance from the optical centre to the vertical axis of the instrument.

q: 222. The multiplying constant for the tacheometer is, generally, kept as
explain: The multiplying constant of a tacheometer is conventionally standardized at 100 for ease of calculation.

q: 223. The value of additive constant for the tacheometer varies from
explain: The additive constant, dependent on the focal length and instrument geometry, typically varies from 0 to about 15 cm for standard tacheometers (approaching zero with an anallatic lens).

q: 224. An angle of deflection right, may be directly obtained by setting the instrument to read
explain: To directly obtain a deflection angle right, the theodolite is set to read 180 degrees when backsighted to the previous station, so that the forward reading directly gives the deflection angle.

q: 225. Left swing is not much favoured in theodolite survey because
options: most of the surveyors are accustomed to right hand
it is inconvenient to turn the telescope anti-clockwise
vertical scale comes to an inconvenient position to be read
explain: Left swing is generally avoided in practice because most surveyors are more accustomed and comfortable operating the instrument with their right hand for a clockwise (right) swing.

q: 226. You have to observe an included angle with better accuracy than what is achievable by vernier, you will prefer the method of
explain: The method of repetition allows an angle to be measured multiple times cumulatively on the graduated circle before reading, effectively increasing the precision beyond the least count of the vernier.

q: 227. Centering error of a theodolite produces an error
options: which does not vary with the direction or pointing
which varies with the direction of pointing and inversely with the length of sight
explain: A centering error causes an angular error that varies depending on the direction of pointing and is inversely proportional to the length of the sight - shorter sights are affected more severely.

q: 228. In horizontal angles, the error due to imperfect leveling of the plate bubble is
options: large when sights are nearly level
explain: The error in horizontal angle measurement due to imperfect plate bubble leveling becomes larger for steeply inclined sights, since the vertical axis tilt has a greater effect when sighting objects at significant vertical angles.

q: 229. Removal of parallax, may be achieved by focusing
explain: Parallax is removed by correctly focusing both the eyepiece (for clear cross-hairs) and the objective (to bring the image into the plane of the cross-hairs).

q: 230. Distance between two stations A and B is 200 m whereas their difference in elevations is 2 m. hence horizontal distance between A and B is
explain: Horizontal distance = sqrt(slope distance^2 - height difference^2) = sqrt(200^2 - 2^2) = sqrt(39996) approximately equal to 199.99 m.

q: 231. Correct length of a 50 m tape, weighing 1.2 kg when a pull of 12 kg is applied at the ends and is freely suspended is
explain: Applying the standard sag correction formula for a tape freely suspended between end supports with its own weight and applied pull, the corrected length works out to approximately 49.96 m.

q: 232. In the double application of principle of reversion, the apparent error is
explain: When the principle of reversion is applied twice (doubled), the apparent error observed becomes four times the actual true error in the instrument's adjustment.

q: 233. Which of the following errors can be eliminated by taking mean of both face observations?
options: Errors due to eccentricity of verniers
Errors due to imperfect adjustments of plate levels
Errors due to line of collimation not being perpendicular to horizontal axis
explain: Taking the mean of face left and face right observations eliminates errors due to the line of collimation not being perfectly perpendicular to the horizontal axis, since this error reverses sign between the two faces.

q: 234. A level line is
options: line parallel to the mean spheriodal surface of earth
line passing through the centers of cross hairs and the center of eye piece
line passing through the objective lens and the eye piece of a dumpy or tilting level
explain: A level line is a curved line that remains parallel to the mean spheroidal (geoid) surface of the earth at every point, distinguishing it from a straight horizontal line.

q: 235. The following sights are taken on the turning point
explain: At a turning (change) point, both a fore sight (to close the previous instrument setup) and a back sight (to begin the next instrument setup) are taken.

q: 236. The adjustment of horizontal cross hair is required particularly when the instrument is used for
explain: Correct adjustment of the horizontal cross hair is important across multiple uses of the instrument - leveling, prolonging straight lines, and measuring horizontal angles - so all of these apply.

q: 237. The two point problem and three point problem are methods of
explain: Both the two-point problem and three-point problem are specific techniques used to solve the resection problem in plane table surveying - determining the plane table's own position from known points.

q: 238. An angle between the inclined line of sight and the horizontal is called
explain: The angle measured between an inclined line of sight and the horizontal plane is, by definition, the vertical angle.

q: 239. The tangent to the liquid surface in a level tube, is parallel to the axis of the bubble
explain: The tangent to the curved liquid surface of the level tube is parallel to the bubble tube's axis specifically at the mid-point of the bubble.

q: 240. The sensitiveness of a level tube decreases if
options: radius of curvature of its inner surface is increased
diameter of the tube is increased
length of the vapor bubble is increased
both viscosity and surface tension are increased
explain: Sensitivity of the level tube decreases when both the viscosity and surface tension of the enclosed liquid are increased, since the bubble then moves more sluggishly in response to tilt.

q: 241. In a constant level tube, size of the bubble remains constant because upper wall is
explain: In a constant-bubble level tube, the upper wall has a relatively larger radius of curvature compared to the main curved surface, which keeps the bubble length constant despite temperature changes.

q: 242. The line normal to the plumb line is known as
explain: A line normal (perpendicular) to the plumb line (direction of gravity) at every point is, by definition, a level line.

q: 243. Long offsets are taken if the offset length exceeds
explain: When an offset exceeds 10 m in length, it is classified as a long offset and requires more careful (instrumental) methods to maintain perpendicularity/accuracy.

q: 244. The angle between two plane mirrors of the optical square is kept
explain: The two plane mirrors of an optical square are set at exactly 45 degrees to each other to achieve the required 90-degree deflection of the sight line.

q: 245. The desirable multiplying and additive constants for a tacheometer
explain: The most desirable (standard) tacheometric constants are a multiplying constant of 100 and an additive constant of 0 m, achieved by using an anallatic lens.

q: 246. Anallatic lens is provided
options: exactly at the line of intersection of vertical and horizontal axes
explain: The anallatic lens is fitted inside the telescope tube, positioned between the diaphragm (cross hairs) and the object glass (objective lens).
